newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar retreats as fund buying fizzles.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar retreats as fund buying fizzles.

text.p: CSCE world sugar prices retreated toward unchanged at midsession, after an early round of fund buying ran into stiff resistance, dealers said.

Spurred by Friday's climb to 10-week highs, commodity funds continued to bid the market higher early Monday. But buying enthusiam lagged after nearby March stalled a notch below Friday's peak of 11.12 cents.
"There was some excellent fund buying leftover from Friday," said one trader. "But technically we failed to get over Friday's highs, so we saw the specs' interest wane."
Sporadic selling by producers and the trade was noted at the highs, traders said, while good buying of the March-May switch provided some support.
At 1133 EST, March futures were down 0.01 cent per lb, at 11.07 cents, having traded from 11.00 to 11.11. Second-position May was up 0.02 cent, while the outer months were down 0.01 to up 0.03.
Turnover was estimated at a steady 10,028 lots as of 1100 EST.
On the charts, traders were watching for a breakout below 10.98 or above 11.12, basis March.
((-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
